sermon.title: Religious Believers in God Can Oppose Both Jesus and God 03/18/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer works through Paul’s sermon in Acts 13. The people and rulers of Jerusalem believed in God but didn’t know him or the scriptures, so they killed the body God lived in. God raised him, witnesses preached even to opponents, all believers are justified, and Paul warned mockers from Habakkuk 1:5. Jealous Jews contradicted and expelled Paul, much as churches today separate over doctrine.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: A garbled minister’s name is marked [unclear] (“Mr. Pentecost”), and an opening verse number is [unclear]. Kept as spoken: “first John 1 chapter 1” for the four stages of growth (14:39). Unverified: 30% of Americans don’t believe in the virgin birth (12:40); over 120 denominations. Sensitive content kept as spoken: “Liberals” insult people, and the Second Amendment: “I don’t care if somebody was shot in high school” (22:51–23:44). Churches lighting candles and using holy water “does nothing” (15:00). Denominations expelled tongue talkers; the pope and the Catholic charismatic movement (23:44–26:30).
